source_acquisition.search_note: The inventory row is no_public_source_found and corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-ddc69d973093/ is absent. The PDF explicitly links https://anonymous.4open.science/r/unlearning-E14D, but the read-only endpoint reports repository_expired/not_connected. gh repo view and recursive-tree checks show crayon-go/machine-unlearning-papers is a catalog and RuntimeErrorz/arxiv-daily is a generic arXiv digest; neither contains a title/ID/author-matched plot, figure, table, LaTeX, notebook, or style source. Strict gh searches for the full title, unlearning-E14D, author phrases, and paper/code identifiers returned no exact visual source. Automatic candidates were therefore rejected and all visual parameters remain PDF rendered estimates.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures 1–3 and 6–14 use coral/red (#F8766D) for Laplace and cyan (#00BFC4) for Gaussian; Figures 4–5 use coral/red for Eps-delta, green (#00BA38) for Gaussian, and blue (#619CFF) for Laplace. Table 1 is black/white booktabs. Color is generally not redundant with shape or line style.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The 38-page PDF, captions, surrounding text, table rules and font objects are vector; embedded plotting content is rendered as mixed/vector-like plot geometry with raster-like sans-serif labels. No public plotting source was found, so plot primitives and exact export format remain rendered estimates.
paper_style.style_consistency: Serif Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern typography is stable across body, caption and Table 1. All plots reuse small sans-serif labels, light gray grids, thin curves, red/cyan semantics, and page-width multi-panel geometry; Figures 4–5 consistently add a three-entry legend.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Comparison of unlearned estimators on new test data: mean GED (with 3 SD error bars) across the dimension p (both in log scale) for Laplace (in red) vs. Gaussian (in cyan). We set λ = 0.5.

color.semantic_mapping: Laplace is coral/red and Gaussian is cyan; each color is reused for its mean line and error bar.

encodings.x: dimension p (six values from 500 to 5000 on a log scale)
encodings.line: solid mean curve with 3-SD vertical error bars
encodings.facet: n=p with m=1, m=5, m=10 from left to right
encodings.text: panel titles, axes, and tick labels

figures.data_and_statistics: GED on 100 previously unseen test observations; λ=0.5, ε=0.75. Mean across 200 replications; m=1 enumerates all single-point removals, while m>1 uses 1000 random removal subsets. Laplace slopes are 0.03, -0.03, -0.01 and Gaussian slopes are -0.47, -0.54, -0.51 in the paper text.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 3.3 GED and Theorem 3 → Section 5 n=p dimension sweep → the figure supports Gaussian GED decreasing at approximately p^-0.5 while one-step Laplace GED remains non-vanishing; Appendix Figure 9 repeats the p slice for n=p/2.
design_strengths: Three m facets share the same log-log grammar and make the p trend comparable.
Error bars show replication variation rather than a single simulated trajectory.
The layout puts the theoretical scaling question directly beside the Section 5 discussion.
design_weaknesses: Caption-only color key and no line-style redundancy make grayscale identification weak.
Small plot labels and error bars are hard to read when the page is reduced.
The text gives slopes but the figure has no slope annotation or theoretical reference curve.
figures.reusable_pattern: For a theoretical scaling claim, fix ε and λ, sweep p on shared log-log axes, facet by deletion size, and show mean plus an explicitly defined uncertainty bar; add a legend or redundant line encoding for standalone use.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Summary of prior certified unlearning notions and per-example loss assumptions, compared to our proposed (φ, ε)-Gaussian certifiability framework (Def. 2). Our notion is optimally achievable with practical Gaussian noise mechanisms in the proportional high-dimensional regime, and it relies on relaxed convex per-example loss assumptions that remain valid in this setting (Sec. 4.2).

tables.uncertainty: None; qualitative taxonomy only, with no estimate, interval, replication, denominator, or failure count.
tables.data_and_statistics: Five qualitative rows: Guo et al. (2020), Sekhari et al. (2021), Allouah et al. (2025b), Zou et al. (2025), and Proposed in this paper. The three columns are related work, certifiability notion/optimality, and high-dimensional applicability; cells state suboptimal/optimal and assumptions fail/extends.
tables.evidence_relation: Section 1 related-work gap and Section 3.2 Gaussian trade-off → Definition 2 and Section 4.2 relaxed loss assumptions → Table 1 taxonomy → Figures 1–5 and Appendix Figures 6–14 test the corresponding GED/UED consequences.
design_strengths: Three semantic columns make work, notion, and high-dimensional applicability scannable.
Black-and-white booktabs rules are print- and grayscale-safe.
The caption states the central optimality and applicability claim.
design_weaknesses: Fails/extends is qualitative and has no operational assumption boundary or sample evidence.
Per-example loss assumptions are mentioned in the caption rather than a dedicated column.
Table text is small at full-page scaling.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a black-and-white three-column theory taxonomy—work, certification definition, applicability—and write qualitative status directly in cells rather than encoding it only with color or rank.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Table 1 establishes the prior-work taxonomy; Figures 1–3 test GED against p, ε, and m in the n=p simulation; Figures 4–5 extend to large p, three noise notions, MNIST, and IMDb; Figures 6–14 add UED, n=p/2, λ=0.2, and removal-set companions. The sequence connects Gaussian certifiability and one-step noisy Newton theory to test-set and unlearned-set evidence.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Most captions begin with “Comparison of …”, identify the metric and sweep, and then specify colors, λ, panels, or 3-SD bars. GED/UED, boxplot statistics, replication counts, and adapted bounds are often deferred to body/appendix text; Figures 8 and 14 are especially short and not independently interpretable.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: The only table is a one-level, three-column related-work taxonomy: related works, certifiability notion (optimality), and high-dimensional applicability. It uses black/white booktabs rules and direct textual status; no performance, cost, failure, or uncertainty columns exist.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Theorem 2 privacy and Theorem 3 GED bounds feed the p/ε/m curves; Figure 4 adds UED and converted comparison bounds, while Figure 5 tests real data. There is no separate visual ablation of Newton steps; method claims are tested through noise-mechanism comparisons and parameter sweeps.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Figures 6, 8, 10, and 14 are UED companions to GED-oriented Figures 1, 3, 9, and 13; Figures 7, 11, and 12 extend the ε/removal-set comparisons; Figures 9–14 repeat the main trends for n=p/2 and λ=0.2. Appendix §I explicitly says these are additional numerical experiments retained for space.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Body, captions, equations, and Table 1 use Nimbus Roman No9 L with Computer Modern math; plot labels use small Helvetica-like sans-serif rendering. The serif/sans division is stable, but plot labels and tick text are small across all 14 figures.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Coral/red and cyan consistently encode Laplace and Gaussian in the two-method figures. Figures 4–5 add green Gaussian and blue Laplace for the three-method comparison with explicit legends. Color lacks shape/linetype redundancy in nearly every plot, reducing grayscale robustness.

most_reusable_patterns: Shared log-log p or m facets with fixed ε/λ and 3-SD error bars for theoretical scaling.
Paired GED/UED figures that keep the same panel, axis, color, and noise semantics while changing only the evaluated data subset.
A black-and-white three-column theory taxonomy that states optimal/suboptimal and high-dimensional applicability directly in cells.
Use of a text legend for the three-noise comparison while preserving a common panel and uncertainty grammar.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1: direct headline p-scaling evidence for Gaussian versus Laplace.
Figure 4: paired GED/UED large-dimensional comparison with three mechanisms.
Figure 5: synthetic-to-real transfer on MNIST and IMDb.
Table 1: compact theoretical taxonomy that frames all later experiments.
Figures 6–14: structurally consistent appendix companions for UED and n=p/2 robustness.
failure_patterns: Captions frequently omit GED/UED definitions, box semantics, replication count, or the most important panel setting.
Most two-series plots have caption-only color keys and no shape/line-style redundancy, weakening grayscale and color-vision accessibility.
Three-panel appendix figures use a two-top/one-centered layout that impedes horizontal comparison.
